overview.headline: Random mating, assortative mating and effects on Hardy-Weinberg balance

keyPoints.point: Random mating is required as a condition for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium but does not always occur in humans
keyPoints.quote: random mating, a condition of HWE (Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium), does not occur

keyPoints.point: Random mating means mating is arbitrary with regard to the locus under study
keyPoints.quote: Random mating implies that mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.

keyPoints.point: Positive assortative mating increases homozygotes while negative assortative mating increases heterozygotes
keyPoints.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.

keyPoints.point: Humans mate randomly for blood type and STR genotype while mating similarly for physical attributes
keyPoints.quote: they mate randomly with respect to other traits such as blood type and short tandem repeat (STR) genotype.

keyTerms.gloss: mating that is arbitrary with regard to the locus
keyTerms.quote: Random mating implies that mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.
This constitutes non-random, positive assortative mating.

keyTerms.gloss: breeding between individuals with dissimilar genotypes
keyTerms.quote: In contrast, negative assortative mating is breeding between individuals with dissimilar genotypes, and is more rare.

keyTerms.gloss: individuals with increased frequency under positive assortative mating
keyTerms.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.

keyTerms.gloss: individuals with increased frequency under negative assortative mating
keyTerms.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.
